title: Credibility of the measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher and contribution to his/her skills development
content:
2.1 Credibility of the measures to enhance the career perspectives and employability of the researcher and contribution to his/her skills development

Overview and structural framing

The career-development and employability measures of this fellowship derive their credibility from three interlocking properties: each measure is grounded in the research work itself rather than being a supplementary layer attached to it; the confirmed pairing of a plant-physiology expert with a geoinformatics and remote-sensing host creates a genuine disciplinary complementarity that structurally requires knowledge transfer in both directions; and the measures cover the full spectrum from highly specialised scientific competences to sector-agnostic transferable skills, broadening the career options of Dr. Rositsa Cholakova inside and outside academia simultaneously. These properties are not asserted generically: they follow directly from the confirmed identity spine of the fellowship — Dr. Rositsa Cholakova as fellow, Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest as host, Dr. András Jung as supervisor — and from the confirmed structure of the research programme (OBJ-1 through OBJ-5, WP1 through WP5).

Dr. Rositsa Cholakova brings to the fellowship approximately four years of post-doctoral experience, a PhD in plant physiology (summa cum laude, 2020) with a thesis directly focused on the non-destructive evaluation of the physiological status of drought-stressed tomato plants (doi:10.2139/ssrn.5492527), and confirmed expertise in non-destructive techniques for evaluating abiotic and biotic plant stress and crop monitoring, photosynthesis under stress, and biostimulants. This profile is characterised by depth in biological ground-truth methods and strength in crop physiology but, prior to the fellowship, limited exposure to the geoinformatics, remote-sensing, probabilistic machine-learning, and Earth-observation data-science infrastructure that the project demands. The fellowship addresses that asymmetry directly, translating it into a structured programme of competence acquisition and genuine two-way knowledge transfer that positions Dr. Cholakova for independent research leadership at the intersection of crop physiology, Earth observation, and uncertainty-aware decision support — a profile that is both academically novel and economically relevant across the agri-technology, environmental-data, and precision-farming sectors.

Governance: the Career Development Plan

The primary governance mechanism for career development is the Career Development Plan (D4-01), prepared jointly by the supervisor Dr. András Jung and Dr. Rositsa Cholakova and submitted as a project deliverable by month 3 of the action. The joint preparation — rather than a plan authored by the host and accepted by the fellow — is deliberate: it encodes the MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 commitment to researcher-centred development and makes the plan a product of the actual competence dialogue between fellow and supervisor rather than a generic institutional template. The Career Development Plan is reviewed and updated during the fellowship to reflect the evolving picture of competences acquired and gaps remaining, ensuring that the governance mechanism tracks the real development trajectory rather than a pre-set script.

Governance within WP4 — Training, supervision and two-way transfer of knowledge, spanning the duration of the fellowship under the lead of Dr. András Jung — provides the institutional backbone within which the Career Development Plan is implemented. Because WP4 runs alongside all three research work packages, training and supervisory activities are structurally interleaved with the research programme rather than concentrated in a dedicated block, ensuring continuous mentoring contact and regular review of the fellow's progress against both scientific and career-development milestones.

The specific quantitative targets for the fellowship — including publication targets, structured training hours, thesis co-supervision commitments, and post-fellowship career milestones — are to be agreed and recorded in the Career Development Plan through the joint dialogue between Dr. Cholakova and Dr. András Jung. No such targets are asserted in advance of that joint agreement: OBJ-5 (Advancement of the fellow's competences and career) explicitly records that specific quantitative targets are to be fixed in the Career Development Plan with the supervisor, reflecting the principle that concrete commitments must arise from the actual supervision relationship rather than being pre-determined independently of it.

Scientific and technical skills acquisition through the research work packages

The technical skills acquired through the project's research work packages are the most direct and credible component of the fellow's career-development programme, because they are demonstrated through deliverables rather than merely declared through training certificates.

Through WP1 — Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the field state — Dr. Cholakova will acquire working competences in multi-sensor Earth-observation data harmonisation (fusing Sentinel-1 SAR, Sentinel-2 optical, and secured PlanetScope imagery with ERA5 meteorological reanalysis and field observations into a unified probabilistic modelling input), probabilistic machine learning (including Bayesian hierarchical models and Gaussian processes that return full posterior distributions rather than point estimates), and the diagnostic methodology of Route B — the homogeneous-patch proxy approach that constitutes the project's confirmed diagnostic route (RQ2) — within a methodological architecture that also defines the rigorous one-step direct probabilistic fusion of Route A as an alternative. These competences represent a substantial methodological expansion beyond the fellow's plant-physiology background: the shift from bench-scale physiological measurement to landscape-scale probabilistic inference from satellite signals is exactly the kind of interdisciplinary crossing that the fellowship is designed to enable, and one that the confirmed disciplinary juxtaposition between fellow and host makes substantive and traceable. This work package produces the Multi-sensor data harmonisation and diagnostic model report (D1-01, due month 14), the technical deliverable that documents and demonstrates the fellow's acquired competence in this domain.

Through WP2 — Uncertainty-aware decision engine and demonstrator integration — the fellow will acquire competences in uncertainty-aware crop-model calibration (specifically the uncertainty-aware calibration of the FAO AquaCrop model that retains an honest parameter posterior rather than collapsing to point estimates, building on established uncertainty-aware crop-model calibration approaches in the literature), counterfactual irrigation simulation over weather ensembles, water-use-efficiency-oriented irrigation recommendation under uncertainty (OBJ-2), and the integration of diagnosis and decision into a standalone research demonstrator — OBJ-4 (Standalone research demonstrator (web MVP)) — at a research prototype level (TRL 3–4, RQ10). The counterfactual-simulation and decision-recommendation methods extend the fellow's scientific toolkit into operational decision science; the demonstrator integration adds software-engineering and system-design competences that are directly valuable in both academic and non-academic career trajectories. This work package produces the Decision engine and research demonstrator report (D2-01, due month 20).

Through WP3 — Field validation, ground truth and uncertainty calibration — the fellow will apply and deepen the non-destructive physiological measurement competences that constitute her pre-fellowship core strength. The RQ4 ground-truth methods — collection of chlorophyll fluorescence, stomatal conductance, canopy/leaf temperature, and spectral reflectance data on Hungarian tomato farms accessed via the associated partner AgroVIR — are used not merely as standalone observational outputs but as the rigorous ground-truth layer of a probabilistic inference system: those measurements are used to assess uncertainty calibration (whether 90% prediction intervals contain the truth about 90% of the time, RQ5), to establish whether pilot success has been achieved (the RQ5 calibration target met on the validation set, RQ7), and to prove or disprove the patch-covariation assumption of Route B through a co-located seasonal measurement campaign that measures the target tomato crop and the proxy patch simultaneously, demonstrating statistical covariation (RQ9). This embedding of established plant-physiology techniques within a structured probabilistic validation framework constitutes a qualitative upgrade of the fellow's pre-existing competences: skills that entered the project as domain expertise leave it as the evidential backbone of an end-to-end uncertainty-quantified system, giving them substantially wider scientific and commercial market value. This work package produces the Field validation and uncertainty calibration report (D3-01, due month 24).

Transferable skills: the MSCA mandatory training dimensions

In parallel to the three research work packages, WP4 (Training, supervision and two-way transfer of knowledge) delivers structured training across the five MSCA Postdoctoral Fellowships 2026 mandatory transferable-skills dimensions. The architecture of WP4 ensures that each dimension is addressed through project-embedded activities wherever possible, making training substantive, auditable, and connected to real scientific outputs rather than self-contained.

Digital and AI skills, including the responsible use of generative AI. The project's methodology is intrinsically computational: probabilistic machine learning, Bayesian inference, counterfactual simulation, and satellite data processing are all areas in which the fellow's competence will deepen substantially through the research work packages themselves. The digital-skills component of WP4 therefore reinforces and contextualises technical skills that are project-necessary rather than supplementary. Training additionally addresses the responsible use of generative AI in the specific context of remote-sensing and crop-water modelling and scientific coding — a dimension that the fellowship's mandatory training framework names explicitly and that the project makes substantive rather than nominal, given the use of probabilistic ML workflows and the production of open research software through WP5.

Knowledge valorisation and innovation/entrepreneurship. OBJ-4 (Standalone research demonstrator (web MVP)) — the integration of the diagnosis and decision engine into an end-to-end research artefact — provides the primary substrate for this training dimension. Dr. Cholakova will develop competences in framing research-prototype outputs in terms of societal utility and user-uptake pathways, working with AgroVIR as the first user-facing interlocutor. AgroVIR's confirmed role — providing farmer access and field-validation feedback at Hungarian tomato farm sites — makes entrepreneurial and valorisation training grounded in real user interaction rather than hypothetical scenarios. Critically, the supervision relationship with Dr. András Jung, who co-founded Cubert GmbH and Brightic Research, brings direct entrepreneurial and industry-founding experience to the mentoring relationship, ensuring that knowledge-valorisation guidance is delivered by a supervisor with personal credibility in the space between academic research and commercial product. This combination of a demonstrator artefact, a real user interlocutor, and an entrepreneurially experienced supervisor makes the knowledge-valorisation training dimension among the most credible of the fellowship's career-development measures.

Research integrity. Research-integrity training is addressed within WP4 as a structured dimension. The training acquires a substantive grounding that goes beyond compliance: the entire methodological spine of the project — from the uncertainty-calibrated diagnosis in OBJ-1 through the honest propagation of uncertainty into the irrigation recommendation in OBJ-2, to the rigorous calibration test and covariation proof of OBJ-3 — is built around intellectual honesty about model limitations. The 90% prediction-interval coverage criterion (RQ5) and the co-located seasonal covariation campaign (RQ9) are both epistemically demanding commitments to honesty that make research-integrity principles a live scientific practice rather than a compliance exercise, directly reinforcing the training.

Open science and FAIR data stewardship. The Data management plan (D5-01, due month 6), produced within WP5 (Dissemination, exploitation, communication and management), is the primary governance artefact for this dimension. Dr. Cholakova will acquire working competences in FAIR data management — making validation datasets, probabilistic model weights, and the research demonstrator code findable, accessible, interoperable, and reusable — as a concrete project activity rather than an abstract training module. Open-access publication of the project's scientific outputs and the open-software posture of the demonstrator extend this training into reproducible research and open-research-software practice, contributing to the call's outcome of regular feedback of research results into the scientific community.

Communication, networking, and public engagement. WP5 (Dissemination, exploitation, communication and management) structures the dissemination and communication activity across the fellowship. Communication activities are directed at two distinct audiences — the host's geoinformatics and remote-sensing scientific community and Hungarian tomato growers reached through AgroVIR — requiring Dr. Cholakova to adjust scientific communication for specialist and non-specialist audiences simultaneously, building the enhanced networking and communication capacities with scientific peers and the general public that the call identifies as a desired outcome (EO-03). The Dissemination and communication activity report (D5-02, due month 24) records the evidence of this engagement across the fellowship's lifetime. The fellowship's international dimension — Dr. Cholakova's move from Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute, Bulgarian Agricultural Academy, Plovdiv, Bulgaria to Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest, Hungary — extends her network across national boundaries and embeds her in a European geoinformatics and remote-sensing research community with broad international reach.

Two-way transfer of knowledge

The two-way transfer mechanism is the most structurally distinctive feature of this fellowship's career-development architecture, because it is genuinely bidirectional rather than a one-directional host-to-fellow transfer. OUT-6 (Enhanced researcher competences and career readiness) is the outcome that the two-way transfer programme targets.

The fellow-to-host direction: Dr. Rositsa Cholakova contributes plant-physiology and non-destructive stress-phenotyping expertise — the biological ground-truth capability that defines the rigour of OBJ-3 (Field validation and honest uncertainty calibration) and that no geoinformatics group can replicate without a plant-physiology collaborator — to the Faculty of Informatics, Institute of Cartography and Geoinformatics at Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest. This contribution is not decorative: without the fellow's RQ4 ground-truth measurement methods (chlorophyll fluorescence, stomatal conductance, canopy/leaf temperature, spectral reflectance), the validation protocol of OBJ-3 would lack the non-destructive physiological layer that gives the uncertainty-calibration test its biological credibility and that makes the project's results relevant to the crop-physiology scientific community as well as the geoinformatics community. The fellow brings a PhD-to-postdoc track record in exactly these methods, applied to drought-stressed tomato — the confirmed crop of the project (RQ1) — making this contribution direct, load-bearing, and evidenced by prior work.

The host-to-fellow direction: the host provides Dr. Cholakova with geoinformatics, remote-sensing, and hyperspectral and multisensor-drone-fusion methods and infrastructure — the satellite-data-processing, probabilistic-modelling, and computational environment in which OBJ-1 (Probabilistic multi-sensor diagnosis of the latent field state) and OBJ-2 (Uncertainty-aware decision engine for water-use-efficient irrigation choice) are built. Dr. András Jung, who leads the Multisensor-Drone-Fusion Working Group (project ELTE TKP2021-NVA-29) and holds habilitations in both Computer Science and Crop Sciences, is positioned to supervise this methodological transfer with direct scientific authority in both the remote-sensing domain (the observation methodology) and the crop-science domain (the biological context) that the project spans. The dual habilitation is particularly significant: it means the supervisor can evaluate the fellow's integration of the two knowledge domains rather than delegating the crop-science supervision to a third party, ensuring that the two-way transfer is governed by a single coherent supervision relationship.

The two-way transfer is managed within WP4 (Training, supervision and two-way transfer of knowledge) and is evidenced through documented methods-exchange activities: Dr. Cholakova teaches non-destructive plant-physiology measurement techniques to the host group, and the host group trains the fellow in remote-sensing image processing, hyperspectral data analysis, and multisensor-fusion methodology. The methods exchange creates an observable, documented record of bidirectional competence transfer that can be audited against the Career Development Plan (D4-01) and the supervisory review record.

International, inter-sectoral, and interdisciplinary dimension

Dr. Cholakova's move from Maritsa Vegetable Crops Research Institute, Bulgarian Agricultural Academy, Plovdiv, Bulgaria to Eötvös Loránd University (ELTE), Budapest, Hungary constitutes a confirmed European Fellowship placement satisfying the MSCA mobility rule. The mobility is not merely geographical: the institutional move takes the fellow from a plant-physiology institute embedded in a national agricultural research system to a Faculty of Informatics within a major central European research university with an international geoinformatics and remote-sensing profile. This change of institutional culture — from domain-specific applied agricultural science to a multidisciplinary informatics-centred academic environment — provides precisely the new mind-sets and approaches to R&I work forged through international, inter-sectoral and interdisciplinary experience that the call identifies as a desired outcome (EO-02). The disciplinary crossing — from crop physiology to geoinformatics and probabilistic machine learning — constitutes an interdisciplinary exposure that expands the fellow's career horizon from a specialist plant-physiology trajectory to a broader precision-agriculture and Earth-observation research profile, with relevance to both academic and applied contexts.

The inter-sectoral dimension is further reinforced by the engagement with AgroVIR as an associated partner: working with a farming-technology entity providing operational field access gives the fellowship an applied-sector dimension that complements the academic research environment of the host, broadening the fellow's professional exposure without requiring a formal secondment.

Contribution to future career perspectives and employability

The skills profile that the fellowship produces — a plant physiologist who can design and run probabilistic multi-sensor diagnostic systems, calibrate uncertainty-aware crop models, validate results against non-destructive physiological ground truth within a rigorous probabilistic framework, and integrate all of this into a research demonstrator — is a profile for which demand exists across multiple sectors and for which the fellowship's research outputs (open-access publications, open research software, validated field data, and the research demonstrator) will provide the independent scientific evidence base.

Within academia, Dr. Cholakova will be positioned for independent research leadership in the precision-agriculture and crop-monitoring field, where the intersection of plant physiology, Earth observation, and probabilistic machine learning remains underexplored and where this project's novelty argument — the end-to-end coupling of learned multimodal fusion, explicit probabilistic crop-water-state estimation, and water-use-efficiency-oriented irrigation decision support — defines a research frontier that the fellow will have directly contributed to establishing. The training in knowledge valorisation and demonstrator development (OBJ-4, WP4) and the research-integrity and open-science competences acquired through D5-01 directly support a trajectory toward ERC-track or national independent-researcher grant instruments. Dr. Jung's supervisory experience and his network across geoinformatics, hyperspectral imaging (Cubert GmbH), and applied research (Brightic Research) provide the fellow with mentored access to the career infrastructure — contacts, publication venues, grant-writing guidance — that independent research leadership requires.

Outside academia, the competence profile is relevant across multiple applied sectors: agricultural-technology firms developing precision-irrigation and crop-monitoring solutions; environmental-data companies processing Sentinel-1/2 and commercial satellite feeds for agricultural decision support; consultancy organisations translating Earth-observation data into farm-management advice; and meteorological or environmental agencies integrating crop-water-stress monitoring into drought early-warning systems. The fellowship's association with AgroVIR — an operational agri-technology entity providing real Hungarian tomato farm access — and the systematic knowledge-valorisation training within WP4, delivered by a supervisor with personal industry-founding experience, make the non-academic career pathway concrete and supported.

The call's primary expected outcome for supported postdoctoral fellows — an increased set of research and transferable skills and competences, leading to improved employability and career prospects within academia and beyond (EO-01) — is addressed comprehensively by the fellowship through the integrated programme of research-embedded skills acquisition across WP1, WP2, and WP3; mandatory transferable-skills training across all five MSCA dimensions within WP4; structured Career Development Plan governance through D4-01; and genuine bidirectional knowledge transfer between a plant-physiology fellow and a geoinformatics and remote-sensing host. The corresponding expected impact of improved employability and career prospects contributing to a stronger and more mobile European research workforce (EI-01) is supported by the confirmed international mobility (Bulgaria to Hungary within the European Research Area), the cross-disciplinary technical profile acquired, and the network extension achieved through integration into the European geoinformatics, remote-sensing, and precision-agriculture research community. The call outcome of enhanced quality and sustainability of research training and supervision (EO-05) is addressed by the structured Career Development Plan prepared and governed jointly by fellow and supervisor, by Dr. Jung's directly relevant dual expertise across Computer Science and Crop Sciences, and by the genuine bidirectionality of the documented knowledge transfer between a plant-physiology expert and a geoinformatics research group.
